notes:
CIRCUIT: a simple two-mesh source-driven network drawn inside a hand-ruled rectangular frame. 50V V-DC (#4) on the left feeds a 3-ohm series resistor (#1) along the top rail y~420; the rail then meets a shunt 6F capacitor (#5) at x~410, continues right through a series 12F capacitor (#0), meets a shunt 0.5H inductor (#3) at x~620, and ends at the 10A I-DC (#2) at x~812. The bottom rail y~630 returns everything and carries the single GND (#6) hanging off it at x~480. 7 components, 4 nets.

NET MAP
  n3 = V-DC #4 top (+) lead + left lead of R #1: the short top-left leg from (130,491) up to (125,420) and right to the resistor.
  n1 = right lead of R #1 + left plate of C #0 (12F) + top plate of C #5 (6F): the top rail from x~362 to x~476, T-junction at (410,414).
  n2 = right plate of C #0 + top lead of L #3 (T at (618,405)) + top lead of I-DC #2: the top rail from x~545 to x~812 and down the right-hand leg into the current source.
  0  = the bottom rail y~630 from x~155 to x~820: V-DC #4 bottom lead, bottom plate of C #5 (T at (431,631)), GND #6 (T at (480,634)), bottom lead of L #3 (T at (641,629)), bottom lead of I-DC #2.

SITE DECISIONS: this sheet has no crossings at all - every intersection is a plain T where a shunt branch meets a rail, so all five CRITICAL sites are junctions and I agreed with the default in each case after looking at the crop.
  S3 (410,414) junction - T, the 6F column drops out of the top rail; nothing continues below the rail on the far side. A crossing reading is not expressible here (degree 3) and would strand C #5's top plate.
  S2 (618,405) junction - T, the 0.5H column drops out of the top rail. Same argument.
  S12 (431,631) junction - T, the 6F column lands on the bottom rail.
  S10 (641,629) junction - T, the 0.5H column lands on the bottom rail.
  S14 (480,634) junction - the GND stub hangs down off the bottom rail (degree 4 only because the GND symbol's top bar is close); the rail passes left-right and the stub goes down. Crossing would leave GND on a net of its own and leave the whole return path ungrounded.
  Non-critical S0 (273,379) and S1 (274,393) are the '3-ohm' handwriting brushing the resistor box; S6 (460,532) is the '6F' handwriting brushing the capacitor. Defaults left alone; they touch no terminal.

PORTS: no fixes needed. Every terminal already sits on a real lead and there are no one-terminal nets. The one flagged spare candidate, V-DC #4 p2@(94,535), is a stroke of the '50V' label to the left of the circle and is correctly unused; #4's t0/t1 are the top (+) and bottom (-) leads. No 3-terminal parts, so no pin ordering to check. Two-terminal order left at default.

CLASSES: all seven agree with the drawing - circle with +/- = V-DC (50V), circle with an up arrow = I-DC (10A), zigzag = Resistor (3 ohm), two parallel plates = Capacitor (12F series, 6F shunt), coil = Inductor (0.5H), hatch = GND.

OTHER INK: the large rectangle from about (12,285) to (1013,738) is a hand-drawn page border, not a conductor. It touches no component and the tracer correctly left it out of every net; confirmed on the re-rendered overview, where the frame is uncoloured.

UNRESOLVED: none. The netlist is unambiguous; no judgement calls were required on this sheet.
